in_hebrew.name: פוטינה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the Hebrew root 'pethach' meaning 'little' and 'el' meaning 'God'. Thus, Fotina can be interpreted as 'God's little one' or 'little one of God'. In the Bible, no such name appears. However, it can be derived from the name 'Petahia' found in the Old Testament.

in_greek.name: Φοτεινα
in_greek.long_meaning: From the Greek word 'phos' meaning 'light' or 'shining' and the suffix '-ina' meaning 'one'. Thus, Fotina can be interpreted as 'bright one' or 'shining one'. In the New Testament, there is no character or saint named Fotina, but it can be derived from the name 'Photina' which is mentioned in the Gospel of Luke (8:3) as a woman who was healed by Jesus.

in_latin.name: Fotina
in_latin.long_meaning: From the Latin word 'fotis' meaning 'bright' or 'shining' and the suffix '-ina'. Thus, Fotina can be interpreted as 'bright one' or 'shining one'. In the Latin Church, there is no saint named Fotina, but it is a variant of the name 'Photina'.
